intro.author: Zephaniah, great-great-grandson of Hizkiah (1:1), possibly King Hezekiah, which would make him of royal descent
intro.written: During King Josiah's reign (640–609 BC), many think before Josiah's reforms of 622 BC
intro.audience: Judah and Jerusalem, with oracles about surrounding nations
intro.setting: After the long, idolatrous reign of King Manasseh, Judah was full of Baal worship, star worship and religious compromise. Young King Josiah would soon launch sweeping reforms. Zephaniah warned that the 'day of the LORD' was near, while Assyria, still powerful, was nearing its collapse.
intro.purpose: To warn of the coming day of the Lord's judgment on Judah and the nations, call the humble to seek God, and promise a purified remnant in whom God would delight.
intro.bigIdea: The day of the LORD brings judgment, but God will rejoice over a humble, cleansed people with singing.

outline.title: The day of the LORD against Judah
Seek the LORD; judgment on the nations
Jerusalem judged and restored with joy
